name: Now Note
job: Tell the reader, in one sentence at the top, what to do now, and let them dismiss it once read; a changed note comes back.

anatomy.role: Bordered row, pill left, sentence, X right
Dot plus `Now`, caps, 0.75em; hidden from screen readers (a hidden `Now: ` prefix reads instead)
Bold lead clause then the action; one sentence
localStorage key = prefix plus a hash of the note text, wrapped in try/catch

states.name: Shown
states.note: First visit, or the text changed since the last dismissal.

states.name: Dismissed
states.note: Hidden on this device for this exact text; focus moved to the next useful control.

use_when: Above the fold, to lead with the reader's next action (`Start with the agreement...`), not a link back to a tab they already saw.
The note changes as the work moves; hashing the text means each new note shows once even if an older one was dismissed.
avoid_when: Do not stack more than one note, or use it for status figures (the status strip holds those).
Do not rely on dismissal for anything important: storage can be blocked, and then the note simply stays.

data.note: The bold clause, such as `Step 1, which you said yes to on November 6.`
The action that follows the lead.
Storage prefix for the page family, such as `myAllyNow`; the hash is appended.
Where focus goes after dismissal (the next control), so it is never lost to the body.

access: `role=note`; the pill is `aria-hidden` and a visually hidden `Now: ` prefix carries its meaning.
The X is a `<button>` named `Dismiss note`, 44px square, with a 2px cyan focus ring.
After dismissal focus moves to a named next control.
Storage reads and writes sit in try/catch; with storage blocked the note just stays visible.

used_by.name: Approved My Ally Step 1 template (public/myally-hub.html, PR 2094)

gates: `kit_specimen.py --check` (in scripts): this page matches its spec.
`kit_primitive_sync.py --check` (in scripts): every page that marks this block carries it unchanged.
Reading-options check: 375 and 1280, light and dark, largest text size, roomy spacing and the easy-read font.
